title: Computed Tomography and Optical Imaging of Osteogenesis-angiogenesis Coupling to Assess Integration of Cranial Bone Autografts and Allografts
protocol: Euthanize 7- to 8-week-old Balb/C mice using CO2 inhalation or intraperitoneal injection of phenobarbital (65 mg/ml; 100 mg/kg).
Confirm the absence of heartbeat and perform cervical dislocation.
Shave the calvarial region using a hair clipper against the direction of hair growth.
Disinfect the carcass head with 70% isopropanol.
Cut the scalp skin using a No. 11 scalpel and remove periosteum.
Use a dental drill and a 4.5-mm inner-diameter trephine to detach a circular fragment of calvarial bone.
Transfer the bone fragment to a 100-mm plastic dish containing sterile saline.
Hold one bone fragment at a time using curved tweezers.
Swab the bone fragment thoroughly using cotton tipped applicator and remove any brain tissue, soft tissue, and blood.
Gently cut away any bone chips that remain attached to the graft using fine scissors so that the graft will have a perfect rounded shape.
Dip each graft once in a 15 ml tube containing 70% ethanol.
Dip each graft twice in 15 ml tubes containing phosphate-buffered saline to wash the ethanol.
Freeze the allografts in a –80 °C refrigerator in cryotubes for at least 1 week.
Sterilize the tips of the surgical tools using a glass bead heater for 30 sec.
Transfer the sterilized tools to a jar containing 70% isopropanol to maintain sterile conditions.
Use sterile gloves during surgery.
Anesthetize a 7- to 8-week-old female mouse by intraperitoneal injection of a ketamine-medetomidine mixture (75 mg/kg and 1 mg/kg, respectively).
Pinch the animal limb to make sure it is deeply anesthetized.
Shave the calvarial region using a hair clipper against the direction of hair growth.
Apply hair-removing cream to remove any fur remnants.
Wipe the area with dry gauze after no longer than 2 minutes.
Wipe again with saline-soaked gauze.
Disinfect the scalp by applying 5% chlorhexidine.
Inject subcutaneously 5 mg/kg carprofen diluted in 200 µl saline.
Apply vet eye ointment to prevent dryness.
Position the animal under the operating binoculars.
Make a 1-cm-long oval cut in the scalp skin using fine scissors and tweezers.
Hold the periosteum using curved tweezers.
Cut away using fine scissors.
Drill the calvarial defect 2 mm anterior to the lambdoid suture using a dental drill and a 5-mm outer-diameter trephine.
Detach the bone fragment using a spatula.
Retrieve the bone fragment and wash it in a 10 mm plastic plate containing 10 ml sterile saline to remove debris.
Do not remove the soft tissues from the bone fragment.
Thaw an allograft in advance, normalize it to room temperature, and then wash it.
Place the bone graft in the defect using curved tweezers so it will not touch the defect margins.
Mix 5 µl of 46 mg/ml fibrinogen with 5 µl of 25 U/ml thrombin to prepare fibrin gel.
Glue the graft to the host bone using the prepared fibrin gel.
Suture the skin using 4-0 vicryl suture.
Apply povidone-iodine to the surgical cut.
Inject 0.25 mg/kg Antisedan to reverse the anesthetic effect of medetomidine.
If the animal does not wake up in 10 min, place it on a warmed pad.
Inject 200 µl sterile saline if needed.
Inject 0.1 mg/kg Antisedan if necessary.
Keep the animals in separated cages for a week to prevent them from opening the sutures.
Place mouse chow soaked in water in a petri dish on the cage floor for a few days post-op.
Inject subcutaneously 200 µl of 1mg/ml Carprofen solution diluted in sterile saline once a day for 3 days after surgery.
Weigh 2,000 U sodium heparin and place it in a 50ml plastic tube.
Add 20 ml saline to the tube containing sodium heparin and shake well.
Fill a 20-ml Luer lock syringe with 15 ml warmed heparinized saline.
Connect the filled syringe to a 23-G scalp vein set.
Affix the syringe to a syringe pump.
Set the syringe pump to pump 10 ml at 1 ml/min.
Sedate a mouse using an intraperitoneal injection of 50µl phenobarbital (65 mg/ml.; 100 mg/kg).
Pinch the animal’s limb to ensure it is deeply sedated.
Secure the mouse on its back to a fixation board wrapped with an absorbent surface liner.
Place the fixed mouse in a fume hood.
Cut the skin from the abdomen to the neck using fine scissors and tweezers.
Cut the abdominal wall up to the xiphoid process.
Cut the rib cage along its lateral aspect, avoiding injury to the lungs and heart.
Use a hemostat to retract the sternum.
Insert the butterfly needle 3 mm into the left ventricle.
Glue the needle to the heart and chest wall using 3-sec glue.
Activate the pump immediately.
Dissect the inferior vena cava to depressurize the vasculature after a minute.
Tilt the board so that liquids will flow away from the head.
Perfuse with heparinized saline until the liver and blood vessels clear.
Perfuse with 10 ml of 4% formaldehyde, avoiding air bubbles and formaldehyde fumes.
Flush out the formaldehyde with 10 ml heparinized saline.
Prepare the radio-opaque contrast agent according to manufacturer instructions.
Mix the compound, diluent, and curing agent using serological pipettes in a 15 ml plastic tube.
Perfuse the animal with the contrast agent mixture at a rate of 1 ml/min.
Observe coronary, intestinal, and hepatic blood vessels for yellowing after perfusion of 2 - 3 ml.
Cut the butterfly needle’s tubing upon completion of perfusion.
Wrap the carcass with toilet paper to prevent leakage to the calvarial region.
Allow polymerization in 4 °C overnight.
Dissect the calvarial region using a scalpel to cut the skin laterally, avoiding damage to the cranial region.
Use fine scissors to cut the cranial bone 10 mm away from the graft.
Scan the isolated calvarial bone sample with a μCT scanner.
Set field of view to 20.5 mm and X-ray energy to 55 kVp.
Set intensity to 145 μA, using 1,000 projections per 360°.
Use an integration time of 200 msec for the scan.
Observe the 2D reconstructed slices generated by the μCT software.
Scan the region of interest to ensure proper coverage.
Locate the calvarial defect within the scanned area.
Assess the quality of perfusion in the sample.
Identify blood vessels successfully (Figure 2J).
Decalcify the sample using 6% Trichloroacetic Acid diluted in Double Distilled Water.
Rescan the sample with parameters indicated in Section 3.10.
Locate the Lambdoid suture in the reconstructed 2D slices.
Define a cylindrical volume of interest (VOI) that is 2 mm high and 8 mm diameter, tangent to the suture.
Segment bone tissue from soft tissues using global thresholding with a lower threshold set to 130.
Apply a constrained 3D Gaussian filter (sigma [σ] = 2.0 and support = 2) to partially suppress noise in the volumes.
Generate a 3D reconstruction of the sample.
Ensure the VOI is properly positioned in the 3D reconstruction (Figure 2K).
Generate a thickness map using the IPL software and the “dt_object_param” function (Figure 2L).
Affix the mouse to the fixation board.
Cut the skin along the abdomen up to the neck.
Cut the abdominal wall along the medial line up to the xiphoid process.
Cut the rib cage laterally.
Insert a butterfly needle into the left ventricle, avoiding the right ventricle.
Affix the needle to the heart and chest wall.
Pump heparinized saline (2-3 ml) into the heart.
Dissect the inferior vena cava.
Perfuse formaldehyde (4%) and wash it out.
Perfuse a yellow-dyed radio-opaque contrast agent.
Confirm clearance of blood vessels, changing color to yellow.
Isolate the calvarial region after polymerization.
Image the sample using a µCT scanner to confirm proper perfusion.
Decalcify the sample.
Rescan the decalcified sample.
Generate a colored thickness map.
Reconstitute probes to a concentration of 2 nmol/100 µl PBS in a 1.5 ml tube.
Pipette gently several times to ensure homogeneous dissolving of the probe.
Take a time-zero image 24 hours before the designated imaging session.
Anesthetize 3 mice using 2 L/min inhalation of 100% medical-grade oxygen supplemented with 3% isoflurane in an induction chamber.
Lower the isoflurane concentration to 1.5% – 2% after proper anesthesia has been established.
Apply vet eye ointment to prevent dryness.
Ensure thermal pad is switched on at all times.
Pinch the animal limb to make sure it is deeply anesthetized.
Do not leave an animal unattended until it regained sufficient consciousness to maintain sternal recumbency.
Shave the calvarial region using a hair clipper applying it against the direction of hair growth.
Remove fur remnants using hair-removing cream.
Place three animals on the IVIS stage warmed to 37 °C for each imaging session.
Set exposure time to auto, view field to C, and adjust filters according to the probe used.
For a bisphosphonate-conjugated fluorescent probe with maximal excitation at 680 nm, use an excitation filter of 675 nm and an emission filter of Cy5.5.
When using a blood-borne fluorescent agent with peak excitation at light wavelength 750 nm, use an excitation filter of 710 nm and an emission filter of 780 nm.
Image the mice through Living Image software by pressing the “Acquire” button.
Ensure the calvarial region is completely visible during imaging.
Allow the mice to awaken inhaling 100% oxygen after imaging.
Inject a 2-nmol fluorescent probe via an intravenous tail injection before the designated imaging session.
Anesthetize the mouse by inhalation of 3% isoflurane for μCT scanning.
Transfer the mouse to the μCT scanner bed and place it in the scanner.
Set the μCT scanner’s x-ray tube potential energy to 55 kVp and intensity of 145 µA at medium resolution.
Perform a scout (single x-ray) scan with a field of view of 20.5 mm, defining a region of interest from the mouse’s eyes to its back skull.
Define a region of interest for the CT scan that extends from the mouse’s eyes to the back of its skull.
Perform a CT scan using 1,000 projections per 360° and an integration time of 200 msec.
Reconstruct the 2D slices using a nominal spatial resolution of 20 µm.
Align the defect margins to a standardized position using μCT software.
Define a cylindrical volume of interest.
Apply the constrained 3D Gaussian filter (σ = 0.8 and support = 1) to partially suppress noise in the volumes.
Segment the bone tissue from soft tissues using a global thresholding procedure.
Determine the volume of mineralized bone tissue in the volume of interest.
Prepare the mouse for imaging as depicted in Sections 4.2-4.4.
Awake the mice by inhalation of 100% oxygen.
Administer 126 mg/kg beetle luciferin to each mouse via intraperitoneal injection.
Return the animal to the induction chamber.
After 2 min, anesthetize the animal using 3% isoflurane.
Place the mice on the IVIS warmed stage.
Set the exposure time to “auto” via Living Image software.
Set the field of view to C.
Image the mice 5 min after luciferin administration.
Define regions of interest because transgene expression varies between mice.
Normalize the calvarial signal to the tail.
